items.text: Starting 1 March 2025, the v2 availability endpoint at api.roamlytics.com will be retired. All clients should migrate to v3, which returns the same fields plus optional rate plans. The old key will stop working after that date, so please update your stored credentials. If you already rotated your password in the developer console, no further action is needed. For questions, email devsupport@roamlytics.com — do not reply to this notice.

intent.requested_action: migrate to the v3 API and update credentials

items.text: Priya consistently exceeded her targets this quarter, and her work on the booking chatbot led to a 12% drop in abandoned carts. Recommended for promotion.
The council voted 7–2 to override the mayor's veto of the short-term rental ordinance. Minutes will be forwarded to the planning office by Friday.

Residents packed the chamber on Tuesday as the city council took up the proposed tourism levy. Most speakers supported a small fee on hotel stays, arguing it would fund sidewalk repairs and a new visitor center. A few hoteliers warned it would push guests toward unincorporated areas.

The council also debated whether to override the planning commission's rejection of the Riverside Hotel expansion. Councilmember Ortega said the project's traffic study was thin, while Councilmember Pratt noted the developer had already addressed parking concerns. The item will return for a final vote on 14 May.

In other business, the city's new chatbot on the permits portal was praised for cutting call volume, though staff admitted it still struggles with questions about outdoor dining permits. Business owners can forward written comments to clerks@fairviewcity.gov by noon on 2 May. Do not reply to the automated confirmation email; it is not monitored.

A full recording and minutes are posted at fairviewcity.gov/council.

Our reservation system's API is being updated this spring, and some older integrations will stop working. If your booking widget uses the legacy endpoint, plan to switch before 30 April. The support team can help with the migration, and the developer docs include a checklist and sample password rotation steps. Many properties have already moved over and report fewer sync errors. Questions go to integrations@staybridge.travel.

intent.requested_action: migrate the booking widget to the new endpoint

items.text: In this year's performance review, the team agreed that the AI assistant feature shipped on time and with strong uptime. Several engineers noted that documentation could be clearer, especially around API key rotation and password resets. The manager recommended a small training budget for the next cycle. Overall the review was positive, with two areas flagged for follow-up.

The city council will meet Thursday to discuss whether to override the recent decision on the airport shuttle contract. Residents who wish to speak should forward their requests to the clerk's office.

The city's new travel chatbot has become an unexpected hit at the visitor center. Staff say it handles routine questions about parking and museum hours, freeing them to help with complex itineraries. One tourist told us she asked it for a rainy-day plan and got a decent list of indoor markets.

Behind the scenes, the chatbot relies on an API that the vendor plans to deprecate in June. The city's IT team is testing a replacement and expects a smooth switch. Meanwhile, council members at Monday's meeting asked whether the tool collects personal data; the vendor says it stores only anonymized queries. Residents with concerns can forward them to privacy@cityofharborview.gov. Do not reply to the chatbot's emailed transcripts, as that address is unmonitored.

A public demo is scheduled for 9 May in the council chamber.
Please note: the booking chatbot cannot reset your account password; use the account settings page instead. Do not reply to this automated message.

intent.requested_action: use the account settings page to reset the password

items.text:
The council's budget committee spent most of Tuesday on the tourism office's request for a new automated booking tool. The vendor promises the system will cut staff time on routine reservations and provide a chatbot for after-hours questions. Committee members were skeptical about the annual fee and asked for a breakdown of the API costs.

A representative from the vendor explained that the older API would be deprecated next year, and that the new system includes password rotation and audit logs. Councilmember Nguyen asked whether residents would still be able to call and speak to a person. The tourism director said yes, and that the chatbot would always offer a handoff to staff.

Public comment was brief. One hotel owner asked the city to forward the contract details to the hospitality association before the vote. The committee deferred the decision to the next meeting and asked staff to override the original three-year term with a one-year pilot. Written comments can go to budget@cityofharborview.gov; do not reply to the automated agenda email.
